title: OpenRAG: An open-source stack for RAG — Phil Nash
talk_summary: Phil Nash presents OpenRAG, an open-source RAG stack combining Docling for document parsing/chunking, OpenSearch for hybrid vector/keyword search, and LangFlow for visual agentic retrieval orchestration. It emphasizes agentic retrieval, filters, MCP/API exposure, and local/offline model options rather than a single fixed top-k pipeline.

takeaways.technique: Agentic retrieval instead of fixed top-k
takeaways.what_they_do: Give the agent the user query plus search tools and let the model decide which searches to run and how many.
takeaways.evidence_quote: With agentic retrieval, we instead give the user's query to a to an agent along with instructions and tools

takeaways.technique: Hybrid vector plus keyword search with filters
takeaways.what_they_do: Use OpenSearch for combined vector and keyword search and expose metadata filters for targeted retrieval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: open rag uses open search for a hybrid vector and keyword search and exposes that sophisticated filtering

takeaways.what_they_do: Docling uses document hierarchy from parsing to produce chunks that preserve structural context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: to produce hierarchically understood chunks of text

takeaways.technique: Expose retrieval as MCP/API for other agents
takeaways.what_they_do: OpenRAG provides an MCP server and API so other agents can call the same retrieval stack.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there is an MCP server available for OpenRag as well as an API

takeaways.what_they_do: The stack can run entirely offline with locally hosted models, including embeddings via Ollama.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the entirety of open rag can be run offline using locally hosted models

takeaways.what_they_do: Use JVector disk-KNN indexing so the vector index does not have to fit entirely in RAM.
takeaways.evidence_quote: because it's based on the disk KNN architecture means your whole index doesn't have to fit in memory
